question.text: Let the abscissae of the two points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> be the roots of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and the ordinates of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> be the roots of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mi>s</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. If the equation of the circle described on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi></math> as diameter is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mfenced><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced><mo>-</mo><mn>11</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>14</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>22</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi></math> is equal to ______.

solution.text:
Let the roots of 2x2-rx+p=0 are x1, x2 and roots of y2-sy-q=0 are y1, y2

So, x1+x2=r2, x1x2=p2, y1+y2=s, y1y2=-q

Equation of the circle with PQ as diameter will be 

x-x1x-x2+y-y1y-y2=0 

i.e. 2x2+y2-rx-2sy+p-2q=0 

On comparing with the given equation r=11,s=7

p-2q=-22

∴ 2r+s-2q+p=22+7-22=7
